Prevention: Reduce handling of and injuries to the plants as this virus is primarily spread through mechanical means
Site nurseries away from older pepper fields and transplant disease free seedlings
Wash hands after handling infected plants with soap and water.
Disinfect farm tools with 10% bleach (sodium hypochlorite) solution after working in infected fields
Remove weeds and alternative hosts (e.g. tomato and egg plant)
Do not smoke and then handle plants before washing hands with soap as the virus can be present in cigarette tobacco
Seedlings should be sprayed with an insectiside before transplanting from nursery (see yellow control column)
Monitoring: Look for symptoms of the disease - infected plant leaves show chlorotic mosaic and distrotion, fruits may be disfigured and plants stunted
Infections can occur at any stage of growth so take action when the first symptoms are seen
Direct Control: Rogue plants showing early symptoms of the disease and destroy in the field
Yellow sticky traps placed at different locations in the field can be used to trap insects
Spray with 5 tablespoons of dishwashing soap in 20 litres of water at 7-14 days intervals (avoid higher concentrations)
Spray neem seed water extract (5% concentration, w/v) to control insects just after their appearance (second and third sprays must be applied at 14 days intervals)
Restrictions: When using a pesticide or botanical, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label
Do not use chemicals with the same mode of action year after year as this can lead to resistance
Always consult the most recent list of registered pesticides of
This viral disease has no chemical control.
Insecticides can be used to manage insect vectors
Spray imidacloprid (200g/L) at 5-7ml/15L of water to control aphids and other insect vectors.
Apply three times at intervals of 7-14 days depending on vector population.
Alternate with other chemical group insecticide after three applications
A quick- acting contact and stomach action pyrethroid, IRAC group: 3A
Apply three times at intervals of 7-14 days
